title: When the Thorn Sings
premise: Beatrix Marchetti has spent six years as the royal taster of Vhalenne, dosing herself with poison until her blood is a fortress, and slipping contraband letters along the smuggler roads of the Thornfells. When a prophecy book written a century ago surfaces bearing tonight's date and the name of her lover, the cartographer Elio Vane, she realizes the old texts have chosen him as the bearer of a secret that could reignite the war between the free cities and the usurper Aurel Kest's empire. Hunted by Kest's inquisitors and betrayed by the crown she serves, Beatrix must decide whether love is a duty she can keep. In the end she drinks the one poison meant for Elio, survives it because of her built immunity, and uses her assumed death to smuggle him and the secret through the Thornfells to the free cities — choosing each other over every crown.
about_author: Vesper Almeida is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working mountain inns along old trade routes before turning to fiction. They write about food, borders, and the people who carry dangerous things across both.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. Opening in the palace kitchens, Beatrix sips a poisoned broth meant for Queen Ilseva, cataloging its bitterness while hiding her fear. Establishes her immunity ritual, her double life, and her exhaustion. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Cartography of a Lie
chapters.summary: Elio POV. Elio finishes a map of the Thornfells for the crown, deliberately omitting three smuggler passes only Beatrix knows. Their secret relationship is shown through coded margin notes. Emotional beat: tenderness built on concealment.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. A black-market bookseller sells her a century-old prophecy codex; tonight's date is inked on its final page beside a man's name: Elio Vane, bearer. She dismisses it as forgery — until the ink is still wet. Emotional beat: dread blooming in the ordinary.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Banquet
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Aurel Kest's envoy attends a state dinner; Beatrix tastes for the queen while the envoy's aide watches her too closely, testing dishes she wasn't asked to taste. Elio is publicly named royal cartographer. Emotional beat: the noose tightening politely.

chapters.title: What the Mountains Keep
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. Beatrix takes Elio through a smuggler pass to hide the codex, showing him her other life. He confesses he's been having dreams of a door beneath the Thornfells — the same door the prophecy names. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening as danger sharpens.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Elio POV. Elio studies the codex and recognizes his own hand in the century-old illustrations. The prophecy's bearer is meant to carry a secret — the location of the Verdant Gate, the ancient treaty-lock between empires. Emotional beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. Beatrix discovers the palace's master poisoner has been logging her doses — someone is building a poison specifically keyed to her immunity, meaning someone knows what she is. Emotional beat: the fortress has a blueprint.

chapters.title: Kestreach
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Summons to Kest's court; the usurper offers Elio a commission to map the Thornfells' depths, revealing he already knows about the Gate. Refusal means suspicion. Emotional beat: power as velvet over iron.

chapters.title: Salt and Silverleaf
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. A quiet chapter: Beatrix and Elio steal a night together before the expedition, cooking a meal from her childhood, trading the truths they've withheld. Emotional beat: love declared in the shadow of duty.

chapters.title: Down the Thorn Road
chapters.summary: Elio POV. The royal expedition enters the mountains with Kest's inquisitor, Sarel Voss, embedded. Elio must mislead them while following the pull of his own dreams. Beatrix shadows the party on smuggler trails. Emotional beat: betrayal performed as loyalty.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elio finds the Verdant Gate — and it opens to his touch, confirming the bloodline the prophecy named. Voss sees everything. Beatrix arrives too late to stop the witnessing. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Voss POV. Inside the inquisitor's head: her faith in Kest, her ambition, and her calculation that the Gate is worth more than her master. She lets Elio live — as leverage. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as a mirror.

chapters.title: The Queen's Poison
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. Returning to the capital, Beatrix is served the keyed poison — meant for her, delivered through the queen's own cup. She survives, and understands the court has known her blood all along. The queen, complicit, begs her silence. Emotional beat: every allegiance is a debt.

chapters.title: Bearer
chapters.summary: Elio POV. Branded bearer and hunted, Elio learns the Gate's secret: it holds back the old war's sealed armies, and Kest intends to open it as a weapon. The secret he must carry is also a burden no one should hold alone. Emotional beat: duty versus self.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Justice
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. Beatrix turns to the Thornfell smuggler network, calling in six years of favors. They agree to move Elio — at a price: the Gate's location, and her loyalty sworn to no crown. Emotional beat: choosing a new family over an old master.

chapters.title: The Long Night of Vhalenne
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Kest's armies march on the free cities; the capital falls into curfew and paranoia. The queen, exposed as a Kest collaborator, orders Beatrix to hand over Elio. Beatrix burns her taster's credentials instead. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Sarel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Voss POV. Voss offers Beatrix a trade: Elio's safe passage for the Gate's opening rite, which she intends to sell to the free cities herself. Beatrix must decide whether an enemy's ambition can be trusted. Emotional beat: alliance as a knife held handle-first.

chapters.title: What the Body Carries
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. Beatrix reveals her full immunity history to Elio — every poison, every year — and the truth that her blood may be the only key that can close the Gate behind them. The prophecy never named a hero; it named a vessel. Emotional beat: love confronting sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Gate Stands Open
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the Gate, Kest's vanguard arrives; Voss turns on both sides, and the sealed armies stir. Elio begins the closing rite but the Gate will only seal from the inside, with blood keyed to old poisons — Beatrix's blood. Emotional beat: the trap of destiny closing.

chapters.title: One Cup
chapters.summary: Beatrix POV. The climax: Beatrix drinks the chalice of keyed poison at the Gate's threshold, her immunity holding long enough to lock the armies in the dark. Kest's vanguard breaks; Voss, choosing the free cities over her master, covers their escape. Elio carries her out. Emotional beat: sacrifice survived by a lifetime of small, stubborn acts.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't Tasted
chapters.summary: Elio POV. Beatrix is declared dead in three kingdoms; her immunity and the rite have left her changed, unrecognizable to royal records. They cross into the free cities as strangers, the secret carried and the Gate silent. Emotional beat: grief and freedom wearing the same face.

chapters.title: When the Thorn Sings
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Epilogue in a free-city kitchen: Beatrix cooks without tasting for anyone's safety but their own; Elio draws new maps with no borders marked. A new codex on the shelf, its last page blank. Emotional beat: love as the only duty they chose.
